t: I should get back to it before somebody notices I stopped.
That is enough standing around for me. I have work waiting.
We can finish this talk after supper.
I had better move before my legs forget how.
Tell me the rest when we both have more time.
I will leave you to your day.
I should go before this becomes an excuse to avoid work.
We have talked longer than I meant to.
I need to see whether anyone has been looking for me.
Let us stop there before we start repeating ourselves.
I will think about that while my hands are busy.
That gives me plenty to consider. I should go.
We should both return to whatever we were neglecting.
I can hear work calling, and it sounds annoyed.
I will catch you later when the day is quieter.
I have kept you long enough.
The rest can wait until tomorrow.
I should check on something before it becomes a problem.
Let me know if you hear anything else.
That is all the talk I have in me today.
I need food more than another opinion right now.
We will solve nothing standing here, but the talk helped.
I should leave before I say something foolish.
There is somebody else I need to speak with.
I understand your point. I am still going to think about it.
We can disagree and still get through the day.
I will not settle this in one conversation.
That is enough serious talk before noon.
I should find some water and clear my head.
All right, I have delayed long enough.
The story sounds different now that I have said it again.
I keep expecting the meaning to become clearer. It has not.
That is what happened. What caused it remains another question.
I believe the first half more than the second.
Some details feel certain. The reason behind them does not.
I have repeated it often enough to hear my own doubts.
Maybe telling it is how I decide what I believe.
I know where I stood. I do not know what stood behind it.
Each person I tell gives me a different explanation.
I thought I understood it until you asked that.
The event was plain enough. Everything around it remains muddy.
I may be remembering my fear as part of the event.
People want certainty from me because I was there.
Seeing it did not make me wiser about it.
I tell the same facts, but I hear them differently each time.
Perhaps the story will settle before I do.
I am certain something changed. I am uncertain who changed it.
The more confident others sound, the more closely I examine my memory.
Part of me believes because the alternative makes less sense.
I wish the facts came with their meaning attached.
That is the account I trust today. Ask me again tomorrow.
I am trying not to improve the story as I repeat it.
I remember the noise better than whatever I thought afterward.
You heard the honest version, including the part I cannot explain.
I tell it because the god's acts should not disappear into ordinary days.
Each telling is another thanks offered aloud.
I remember it clearly because the god made it clear.
People should know when the god reaches into our lives.
I will keep telling it while anyone still doubts.
The important part is not my fear. It is what the god did.
I have checked every detail against what I remember.
The story belongs to everyone who lives under this god.
I repeat it so gratitude outlasts surprise.
What I saw strengthened my faith. Telling it may strengthen yours.
I will not soften the god's power to make anyone comfortable.
That memory reminds me why I still kneel.
I tell the event plainly because people keep adding divine reasons.
The strangest part is how quickly the story grew afterward.
I was there. Most people correcting me were not.
Nothing improves a rumour faster than a frightened audience.
I keep the facts short so nobody mistakes them for worship.
Every retelling gains certainty that the first witness never had.
I remember confusion. Other people remember a divine plan.
The event needs no god to remain unusual.
I have corrected that detail so often I am tired of hearing it.
Believe the event if you like. Question the explanation.
I saw what happened, not who supposedly wanted it.
That is the plain account. The shrine has a longer one.
I need time alone before I decide what that means.
Let us stop before borrowed certainty becomes my own.
I heard you. Believing you may take longer.
I am leaving with more questions, but better ones.
Thank you. I will remember what the god has shown us.
We should bring that account to the shrine.
I have heard enough to offer thanks tonight.
May the god keep you. I should return to work.
We will disagree again later. I have work now.
Keep the facts. I will leave the faith to you.
That explanation does not improve with another telling.
I understand the story. I still reject the conclusion.
A new child is enough good news for one conversation.
I should visit the family instead of discussing them all day.
Let the mother rest. We have repeated this enough.
I will bring something useful when I go to see them.
The god protected them. I will give thanks and let them rest.
That child entered the village under a blessing. Remember it.
I hope it was help. I know the family needs quiet now.
Maybe the birth means something. I will decide after the excitement settles.
Praise the people who worked. I am done discussing invisible help.
Mother and child survived. That conclusion is enough.
A person was struck. I do not want to make light of it.
We should stop talking and check whether anyone needs help.
The warning is clear enough. I am going to the shrine.
I need time before I call that justice.
Lightning killed someone. I will not turn death into a lesson.
The field is fuller. We should gather before weather changes.
Good news wastes daylight when we stand around repeating it.
I will thank the god after we bring the harvest in.
Maybe it was a blessing. Either way, the crop needs hands.
Call it whatever you like after the work is finished.
I should return before the lamp burns lower.
We can talk above ground when the load is out.
The stone will not move while I stand here talking.
I need daylight if I am going to check those tracks.
Save the rest until I return from the trail.
The animals will not wait for this conversation.
I should fill the basket before somebody finds my patch.
We can continue while sorting what I bring back.
The berries are not going to pick themselves.
I have duties at the shrine before dusk.
Bring that question to me after the evening prayer.
I should listen to the next person before offering another answer.
I need to finish the marked trees before the light goes.
We can argue after the timber is stacked.
The axe is waiting, and it has more patience than I do.
